newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end sharply down on Iraq news.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end sharply down on Iraq news.

text.p: Share prices closed sharply lower as investors reacted to news of a U.S. missile attack on Iraq, dealers said.
But analysts believed the impact would only be short-term.

"I don't think it's going to prolong at all," said Laurence Lau, head of research at Jupiter Securities. "I'm not surprised if the Dow moved up tonight. The Composite Index could go back to 1,100 tomorrow."
The benchmark Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index ended down 12.88 points or 1.16 percent at 1,093.32, after hitting a low of 1,086.49 in early afternoon trade.
Analysts said news of the Iraq attack added gloom to a market undergoing consolidation and lacking other leads.
"There's not enough good news...and the market is due for a correction," said Audrey Ho, head of research at Mohaiyani Research.
Blue chips have also been under some selling pressure amid renewed fears of monetary tightening in Malaysia following stronger money supply growth in July.
The punter-dominated Second Board index fell 13.89 points or 2.59 percent to 522.57.
